testCase.name: [local] S08 Status sort × every status, both contexts: same label stays together, ties in room order

descriptionHtml:
Case priority: P0 · stated in the UAT / ticket AC · TFA-92581 AC 4; UAT TC-03 step 5 · “Sort correctly reorders the list by room, name, and status, with room as the primary sort”. Mixed: stated part — Same visible status label forms one block under the status sort; our part — Records with no stored status and room order inside each block (only the stated part makes a QA bug).

Suggestion B31 · new · not counted as a bug (was S2): Our own extended check (not stated in the UAT or a ticket AC): Nearest line only: TFA-92581 AC 4 / UAT TC-03 step 5; the split needs a patient row with no stored status, which no app create path writes (API or old data only)

Sorting by status splits one status into two blocks: a patient with no stored status shows the pending label ('Not Yet Prepped' in Hospital, 'Pending' in Nursing Home) but is sorted with 'Pre-Rounded'; the same cause puts room 402 before room 2 in Hospital room order

Tickets: TFA-92581 ready for qa · counts as a QA bug: yes · found on: dev

Note: Cause: patientList.ts:123 ranks a missing status like Pre-Rounded. Every create path in the app writes 'pending', so a row with no status only comes from the API or old data.

Approach · TC-03 Search & Sort · S08 Status sort × every status, both contexts: same label stays together, ties in room order

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U2 Hospital: sort by room, by name and by status each puts the list in the correct order. (UAT TC-03; TFA-92581 AC 4; TFA-92581 AC 5)
  • U7 Nursing Home: sort by room (unit/room), by name and by status each puts the residents in the correct order. (UAT TC-03; TFA-92581 AC 4; TFA-92581 AC 6)

Test design technique: Decision table (decision-table) — List the combinations of several conditions and check each one, to see that the result follows the rule.

Given Hospital: two patients per status in a low and a high room: pending 1/21, no status 2/22, pre-rounded 3/23, seen 4/24, in-encounter 5/25, note-ready 6/26, post-rounded 7/27, complete 8/28. Nursing Home, all on Today's Visits: pending, no status, pre-rounded, in-encounter, note-ready, complete, post-rounded on units 'R …

When On the Hospital list choose the status sort and load every patient; on Nursing Home Today's Visits choose the status sort; then open All Residents with the status sort

Then Cards with the same visible status label form one contiguous block: Hospital Not Yet Prepped (pending + no status), Pre-Rounded, Seen (seen + in-encounter), Note Ready, Complete (post-rounded + complete); NH Pending (pending + no status), Pre-Rounded, In Visit, Note Ready, Complete (complete + post-rounded). Inside each block the rooms ascend

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): Judged now on a Q4-independent invariant (U2, U7): labelGroupsContiguous and roomAscendingWithinLabel per checkpoint. The absolute order of the blocks is recorded for Q4, not judged. Predicted from code: Fail. A no-status record sorts with Pre-Rounded (STATUS_RANK[''] ?? 1) but shows Not Yet Prepped / Pending, so that block is split

Where it ran: local newspec-c (new Playwright specs); test method PW · Playwright script; lane planned in the matrix: existing tests (Tim's Playwright) (automated)

S08 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/TC-03.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Triage (2026-10-14): 1 row.

Issue type: New product issue · environment local · tickets TFA-92581 ready for qa

Sorting by status splits one visible status into two blocks: patients with no stored status show 'Not Yet Prepped' or 'Pending' but sort among 'Pre-Rounded', so the same label appears in two places on the Hospital and both Nursing Home lists.

Evidence: datasets lane (status dataset): Hospital blocks are NYP×5, PR×1, NYP×1, PR×2…, with the same split on NH Today and All. The cause is the STATUS_RANK[''] ?? 1 fallback; snf:add and rounding:add store no status when the client omits it. This was predicted in the TC-03 risks and the Q4 text mentions the code fact, but it is not in the dev report, ledger or knownGaps. It fails the Q4-independent invariant. The block order itself is only recorded, for Q4.

Environment: local — main e02167f → 8b4be94a (10-20), local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane newspec-c.

Test method: PW · Playwright script (PW (labelGroupsContiguous / roomAscendingWithinLabel on card order)); secondary: CODEREVIEW · Code review — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on both; Source: newspec-c.
